risks.title: Increased credit risk on NDFI loans
risks.score_rationale: Risk is highlighted as new and material with classified credit ratio declining from 5.5% to 0.8% but accompanied by an exceptional charge of $50M in 2025 due to irregularities. The amount at stake and strong language (irregularities and litigation) indicate an existential risk. The Credit category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Commercial real estate risk concentration
risks.score_rationale: Real estate portfolio (CRE) represents $13.4 billion with a 22% decline in construction loans. Risk is repeated across multiple sections with mention of LTV, collateral, and enhanced monitoring. Language reflects elevated vigilance given market deterioration. Credit category carries high weight.

risks.title: Geographic and sector concentration risk
risks.score_rationale: Text explicitly mentions concentration management by sector (e.g., energy, real estate) and geography (Texas, California). These risks are structured within the ERM framework and actively monitored. Language is precise and repetitive, indicating sustained concern.

risks.title: Dependence on economic conditions and interest rates
risks.score_rationale: Text repeatedly cites sensitivity to interest rates and economic conditions (e.g., stress scenarios). This risk is embedded in cash flow and collateral analysis. Language is recurring and serious, with no marked change versus prior year.

risks.title: Risks related to government-guaranteed loans
risks.score_rationale: Guaranteed loans (SBA, etc.) represent $801M, with high guarantee coverage (77%). Risk is moderate but highlighted as specific, with dependence on federal rules. Language is factual, without particular emphasis, but the Regulation category adds weight.

risks.title: Deficiencies in collateral control and appraisals
risks.score_rationale: Text emphasizes appraisal, inspection, and revaluation requirements, particularly for real estate. Risk is linked to underlying asset quality and valuation methodologies. Language is technical and repetitive, indicating a key operational issue.

ai_positioning.summary: Zions does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.
